text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's public construction and national housing ministry halted some home construction projects under a pay-for-your-house scheme and diverted the money towards building First Lady Grace Mugabe's Z$6 million mansion in Harare's Borrowdale suburb.
- The Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) pension fund has to date recovered Z$7.6 million from an initial capital of Z$23.7 million in investments funds.

- The National Social Security Authority (NSSA) -- whose income from member contributions since it commenced business in 1994 currently stands at Z$1.44 billion -- has acquired a large parcel of shares in Meikles Africa.

- Hundreds of prospective Zimbabwean "money makers" -- swindled out of millions of dollars by bogus savings clubs -- besieged Harare central police on Thursday demanding refunds from club officials who had taken refuge there.
- Construction of the new Z$1 billion international passenger terminal at Harare Airport is expected to soon begin after the government awarded the contract to a Cypriot company.
